questions.question: Why are Group 0 elements referred to as unreactive?
options: They easily lose electrons to other elements
They have a full outer shell and do not readily react
They exist only as single atoms at extremely high temperatures
They form highly acidic solutions in water

questions.question: What is the physical state of all Group 0 noble gases at room temperature?
options: Solid
Liquid
Gas
Plasma

questions.question: What atomic feature makes the noble gases in Group 0 highly stable?
options: They have incomplete inner electron shells
They have complete outer electron shells
They have an odd number of protons
They form covalent bonds with each other

questions.question: What trend is observed as you move down Group 0 of the periodic table?
options: Atomic mass, density, and boiling points increase
Atomic mass decreases but density increases
Boiling points decrease as density increases
Density decreases while atomic mass increases

questions.question: How do the chemical and physical properties of elements generally change as you go down a group in the periodic table?
options: They change randomly from element to element
They remain completely identical for every element
They change gradually down the group
They reverse their order at every second element

questions.question: Which of the following is a physical property characteristic of Group 1 metals?
options: They are extremely hard and brittle
They are soft and have lower densities than most other metals
They have much higher densities than transition metals
They become less reactive as you go down the group

questions.question: Why are Group 1 metals specifically referred to as the alkali metals?
options: Because they react with water to form an alkaline solution and hydrogen gas
Because they react with oxygen to form acidic liquids
Because they can only exist in alkaline environments
Because they release acidic vapours when heated

questions.question: What products are formed when Group 2 metals react with dilute acids?
options: An oxide and water
A salt and hydrogen gas
A hydroxide and oxygen gas
A salt and carbon dioxide

questions.question: How does the reactivity of Group 2 metals compare to Group 1 metals in the same period?
options: Group 2 metals are more reactive than Group 1 metals
Group 2 metals have identical reactivity to Group 1 metals
Group 2 metals are less reactive than Group 1 metals
Group 2 metals do not react, unlike Group 1 metals

questions.question: Which of the following describes the elements found in Group 7?
options: They are all metals with bright, shiny surfaces
They are unreactive gases with no colour
They are all non-metals that have coloured, mostly toxic vapours
They are highly conductive liquids at room temperature

questions.question: What change in state occurs for Group 7 elements at room temperature as you move down the group?
options: From solid to liquid to gas
From gas to solid
From liquid to gas
They all remain solids at room temperature

questions.question: What is the trend in reactivity as you move down Group 7 of the periodic table?
options: Reactivity increases
Reactivity decreases
Reactivity remains constant
Reactivity increases then decreases

questions.question: What type of compound is formed when halogens react with Group 1 and 2 metals?
options: Metal oxides
Metal hydroxides
Metal halides
Metal carbonates

questions.question: What is a common property of the metal halides formed by reactions with halogens?
options: They are completely insoluble in water
They are soluble in water
They only dissolve in concentrated acids
They form insoluble gaseous precipitates

questions.question: In the periodic table, what are the vertical columns and horizontal rows called?
options: Columns are called periods, and rows are called groups
Columns are called groups, and rows are called periods
Columns are called families, and rows are called categories
Columns are called series, and rows are called grids

questions.question: Which Russian scientist is credited with developing the periodic table?
options: Dimitri Mendeleev
Antoine Lavoisier
John Dalton
Ernest Rutherford

questions.question: How are all the elements organised in the periodic table?
options: By their alphabetical names and date of discovery
Into groups and periods, according to their properties
By their state of matter at absolute zero only
Randomly, to keep similar elements separated

questions.question: What can be said about elements that belong to the same group in the periodic table?
options: They have completely different chemical properties
They have similar properties
They always have the same physical state at any temperature
They have the exact same atomic mass

questions.question: Apart from groups and periods, how can the elements of the periodic table be broadly divided?
options: Into non-metals and metals, which include the transition metals
Into synthetic and organic elements only
Into gases and liquids only
Into acids and bases only
